questions.stem: Which of the following is a legitimate, beneficial use of AI described in the review?

choices.text: Summarizing thousands of emails and sifting security logs for hidden threats
Generating application code a developer doesn't understand

questions.explanation: AI is used to generate content, summarize thousands of emails in seconds, and sift terabytes of security logs to find threats hidden from human eyes.
questions.trap: Deepfakes, uncited papers, and ignorant code are listed as inappropriate uses - the legitimate one is analysis/summarization.

questions.stem: Which inappropriate use of AI is identified as the most dangerous, where AI impersonates a real person?
questions.explanation: The most dangerous inappropriate use is fraud, specifically deepfakes, where AI impersonates a real person.
questions.trap: Plagiarism and ignorant code are also misuse, but the review singles out deepfakes/fraud as the most dangerous.

questions.stem: Students using AI to write papers without citation is an example of which inappropriate use?
questions.explanation: Using AI to write papers without citation is plagiarism.
questions.trap: Hallucination and bias are AI limitations, not the act of passing off AI work as your own - that's plagiarism.

questions.stem: A developer generates application code from AI that they don't understand. Why is this a concern?

choices.text: It always runs faster than hand-written code
It guarantees the code is bug-free
It can only be written in Python
It can introduce bugs or vulnerabilities they can't evaluate

questions.explanation: Generating code you don't understand ('ignorant code') can introduce bugs or vulnerabilities you're unable to catch or evaluate.
questions.trap: AI-generated code is not automatically faster or bug-free; the risk is unreviewed flaws.

questions.stem: An AI trained on a resume dataset dominated by men starts unfairly rejecting female applicants. Which AI limitation is this?
questions.explanation: Feeding AI flawed data (a male-dominated resume set) teaches it that bias, so it unfairly rejects female applicants - a funhouse mirror reflecting a distorted reality.
questions.trap: Hallucination is confidently inventing false facts; learning unfairness from skewed training data is bias.

questions.stem: An AI confidently invents historical facts that never happened. Which limitation is this?
questions.explanation: A hallucination is when AI is confidently incorrect - it might insist a cloud is a dog or invent historical facts that never happened.
questions.trap: Bias comes from skewed training data; confidently fabricating facts is a hallucination.

questions.stem: Public AI (like a public chatbot) is compared to a public library. What is its main security risk?

choices.text: Sensitive data you type in could be exposed to others
It knows too little to be useful

questions.explanation: Public AI has massive knowledge but is open to the world, so sensitive data you type in (passwords, company secrets) might be exposed to others - a high security risk.
questions.trap: Public AI's problem is over-exposure of your data, not a lack of knowledge - it's very knowledgeable.

questions.stem: Private AI is compared to a company vault. What is its main trade-off versus public AI?

choices.text: It is secure and controlled but only knows what you put inside, limiting its scope
It is less secure but knows everything
It exposes your data to the public internet
It cannot be controlled by the company

questions.explanation: Private AI is secure and controlled, but it only knows what you put inside it, which limits its scope.
questions.trap: Private AI trades breadth for control; it does NOT expose your data publicly - that's the public-AI risk.

questions.stem: An employee needs to analyze a document containing confidential company secrets with AI. Which option best protects the data?

choices.text: Paste it into a public chatbot for the best accuracy
Email it to an AI vendor
Use a private (in-house) AI that keeps data controlled
Post it to a public forum for crowd analysis

questions.explanation: For confidential data, a private AI keeps everything secure and controlled, avoiding the exposure risk of public AI.
questions.trap: Public chatbots and forums risk leaking the secrets to others; private AI is the controlled choice.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly summarizes the two core AI limitations the review says to watch out for?
questions.explanation: AI is powerful for automation and analysis, but watch out for bias (learned from flawed data) and hallucinations (confidently incorrect output).
questions.trap: Scalability and high availability are cloud traits; the AI limitations to watch are bias and hallucinations.
